newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-EMI to return some 500 million stg.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-EMI to return some 500 million stg.

text.p: EMI is planning to return some 500 million stg in cash to its shareholders, chairman Sir Colin Southgate told Reuters on Tuesday.
Southgate said the strength of sterling was likely to depress earnings by around 30 million stg in the current financial year, with most of the impact felt in the first half.
The EMI chairman repeated that the company was not involved in merger talks with Seagram, the Canadian drinks and entertainment group, or any other party.
Southgate said the capital return was a large sum but he said that the company had looked at what it needed for its EMI and HMV operations.

He said EMI's interest cover was 21 times and that shareholders would "have beaten him around the head" if that level had been maintained. It should be around six or seven times after the return of capital.
The EMI chairman confirmed that Charles Koppelman, head of EMI-Capitol Music Group North America was leaving the company along with fellow U.S. executive Terri Santisi.

"We have removed one layer of management although we are not touching the labels," he said of the North American restructuring which the company announced on Tuesday. Southgate said that the move would cut costs, improve integration and bring some fresh blood into senior management.
"This is the beginning of a three-year plan," he said, adding that he planned to step down as chairman in July 2000.
Southgate said there was nothing wrong with the company's operating results.
Pre-tax profit excluding exceptional items rose 3.6 percent to 380.5 million pounds while the company raised full year dividend by 11 percent to 30 pence per share.
Pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit would have totalled 410.1 million stg at constant rates of exchange.
The company forecast modest progress this year because of the strength of sterling and subdued industry conditions.

Southgate said he ultimately expected a return to a seven to eight percent growth in the global music market but added that this would not happen this year. He said growth of three to four percent was more likely in 1997.
Asked about newspaper reports of merger talks between EMI and Seagram, Southgate said he hadn't spoken to Seagram chief Edgar Bronfman since last October and that last meeting was a social occasion.
"There are no merger talks with anyone," said Southgate.
